text: fit_me_calibration() estimates classical multivariate measurement-error model Wj=α0j+α1jX+ej,e∼𝒩J(0,Σe), W_j = \alpha_{0j} + \alpha_{1j}\, X + e_j, \qquad e \sim \mathcal N_J(0, \Sigma_e), validation sample, returning per-surrogate intercepts slopes together residual covariance Sigma_e. slope alpha1 near 1 indicates essentially unbiased surrogate; departures 1 flag scale shift GLS step correct. gls_combine() applies per-surrogate back-transform W_tilde_j = (W_j - alpha_{0j}) / alpha_{1j} collapses back-transformed surrogates GLS weights omega = Sigma_tilde^{-1} 1 / (1' Sigma_tilde^{-1} 1). combined exposure W_bar minimum-variance linear unbiased estimator X available surrogates, conditional variance sigma_w_sq residual variance SIMEX needs next step.

title: Quick start: AFT + spline + SIMEX
text: SIMEX (simulation-extrapolation) corrects bias arises fitting AFT-spline noisy W_bar instead unobserved X. value lambda adds extra Gaussian noise variance lambda * sigma_w_sq W_bar, refits dose-response B times, finally extrapolates per-lambda curves back lambda = -1 (zero-error case). Key knobs: lambda — perturbation grid. typical choice c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2); including values gives stable quadratic extrapolation. B — number Monte-Carlo perturbations per lambda. Small B (say 10–20) enough quick look visibly noisy; B = 100 practical floor publication-quality point estimate. v_ref — reference values adjustment covariates dose-response reported (curve invariant choice vertical shift, remove anchoring first grid point). summary() reports configuration fit alongside SIMEX-corrected dose-response quantiles exposure grid, naive curve smoothing-bias reference. Correction row quantifies much SIMEX shifts naive curve exposure quantile – larger magnitude indicates residual attenuation correction undoing. bare plot() SIMEX object draws corrected curve naive curve overlaid (smoothing-bias reference). simulated data can also pass truth overlay data-generating curve dashed line; real data simply omit .

code: SC <- list(x_mean = log(300), x_sd = 0.45,            f_args = list(x_min = log(150), alpha = 3.0, beta = 0.6))  f_min     <- function(x) do.call(f_true, c(list(x), SC$f_args)) x_grid_m  <- seq(qnorm(0.05, SC$x_mean, SC$x_sd),                  qnorm(0.95, SC$x_mean, SC$x_sd), length.out = 80) truth_m   <- f_min(x_grid_m) - f_min(x_grid_m[1])  N_REP_M <- 10L        # small for a fast build; raise locally for the manuscript N_M     <- 1200 N_VAL_M <- 350  ise_of <- function(curve) {   e  <- curve - truth_m   dx <- diff(x_grid_m)   sum(((e[-1] + e[-length(e)])^2 / 4) * dx) }

title: Simulation study: Oracle vs Naive vs SIMEX
text: well SIMEX recover curve surrogate gets noisier? sweep mean per-surrogate reliability 0.5, 0.65, 0.8 (poor -> good), holding everything else fixed; sigma_u_for_reliability() returns matching measurement-error covariance. reliability falls, Naive ISE inflates sharply worsening attenuation, SIMEX removes large part excess – roughly halving Naive ISE reliability 0.5. gain shrinks reliability improves: 0.8 naive attenuation already small, correction little left (extrapolation variance can offset tiny remaining bias). SIMEX earns keep measurement poorest.
code: run_full <- function(seed, Sigma_u) {   sim <- generate_aft_data(n = N_M, n_val = N_VAL_M, Sigma_u = Sigma_u,                            x_mean = SC$x_mean, x_sd = SC$x_sd,                            f_args = SC$f_args, seed = seed)   cal <- fit_me_calibration(sim$validation)   W   <- as.matrix(sim$survival[, cal$W_cols])   g   <- gls_combine(W, cal)   dat <- sim$survival; dat$W_bar <- g$W_bar    fo <- fit_aft_spline(dat, "X_true", covariates = names(V_REF), df = DF)   fn <- fit_aft_spline(dat, "W_bar",  covariates = names(V_REF), df = DF)   lo <- predict_curve(fo, x_grid_m, V_REF, "X_true")   ln <- predict_curve(fn, x_grid_m, V_REF, "W_bar")   s  <- simex_aft_spline(dat, "W_bar", sigma_w_sq = g$sigma_w_sq,                          covariates = names(V_REF), v_ref = V_REF,                          lambda = LAMBDA, B = B_INNER, x_grid = x_grid_m)   list(Oracle = lo - lo[1], Naive = ln - ln[1], SIMEX = s$curve_simex) }  rel_levels <- c(0.5, 0.65, 0.8) sweep <- t(sapply(rel_levels, function(r) {   Su  <- sigma_u_for_reliability(r, var_x = SC$x_sd^2)   rep <- lapply(seq_len(N_REP_M), function(i) run_full(70000L + i, Su))   vapply(methods, function(m) mean(vapply(rep, function(z) ise_of(z[[m]]), 0)),          numeric(1)) })) rownames(sweep) <- sprintf("reliability = %.2f", rel_levels) round(sweep, 3) #>                    Oracle Naive SIMEX #> reliability = 0.50  0.025 0.107 0.058 #> reliability = 0.65  0.025 0.068 0.036 #> reliability = 0.80  0.025 0.044 0.029

title: Simulation study: Oracle vs Naive vs SIMEX
text: GLS combiner pools three surrogates. give surrogates distinctly different quality (relative error variances 1 : 3 : 6, mean reliability 0.65 spanning roughly 0.84 0.47) run estimator surrogate alone (surrogate_pattern = "^W1$", etc.) combiner. uses existing surrogate_pattern argument – engine change. single-surrogate ISE ranks reliability (W1 best, W3 noisiest), combiner sits even best single channel – payoff pooling correlated measurements.
code: patterns <- c(W1 = "^W1$", W2 = "^W2$", W3 = "^W3$", Combined = "^W[0-9]+$") Su_mid   <- sigma_u_for_reliability(0.65, var_x = SC$x_sd^2, ratios = c(1, 3, 6))  ladder_curves <- lapply(seq_len(N_REP_M), function(i) {   sim <- generate_aft_data(n = N_M, n_val = N_VAL_M, Sigma_u = Su_mid,                            x_mean = SC$x_mean, x_sd = SC$x_sd,                            f_args = SC$f_args, seed = 80000L + i)   sapply(patterns, function(p) {     cal <- fit_me_calibration(sim$validation, surrogate_pattern = p)     W   <- as.matrix(sim$survival[, cal$W_cols, drop = FALSE])     g   <- gls_combine(W, cal)     dat <- sim$survival; dat$W_bar <- g$W_bar     s   <- simex_aft_spline(dat, "W_bar", sigma_w_sq = g$sigma_w_sq,                             covariates = names(V_REF), v_ref = V_REF,                             lambda = LAMBDA, B = B_INNER, x_grid = x_grid_m)     s$curve_simex   }) })  ladder_ise <- rowMeans(sapply(ladder_curves,                               function(M) apply(M, 2, ise_of))) data.frame(SIMEX_ISE = round(ladder_ise, 3)) #>          SIMEX_ISE #> W1           0.027 #> W2           0.060 #> W3           0.087 #> Combined     0.033 mean_ladder <- sapply(names(patterns), function(nm)   rowMeans(sapply(ladder_curves, function(M) M[, nm])))  pal <- stagill_palette() ladder_cols <- c(W1 = unname(pal["MutedTeal"]),                  W2 = unname(pal["ApricotCream"]),                  W3 = unname(pal["BurntPeach"]),                  Combined = unname(pal["TwilightIndigo"]))  plot_curves(x_grid_m, truth_m,             fits = as.list(as.data.frame(mean_ladder)),             colors = ladder_cols,             x_lab = "Daily LPA (minutes)",             title = "Per-surrogate ladder: single channels vs the GLS combiner")

title: AFT + Spline + SIMEX for Nonlinear Dose-Response with Multivariate Measurement Error
text: aftsplex implements two-phase estimator: Phase 1. Multivariate linear measurement-error calibration external validation sample paired (truth, surrogate) observations: log W*_ij = alpha_0j + alpha_1j * log W_i + e_ij. GLS combiner weights back-transformed surrogates single calibrated exposure conditional variance. Phase 2. Natural-cubic-spline AFT model calibrated exposure, corrected residual attenuation via SIMEX (Cook Stefanski, 1994). text: Robustness fixes surfaced adversarial stress-test 0.3.0. changes input guards bug fix; valid-input behaviour byte-identical generate_aft_data() baseline unchanged. two_stage_bootstrap() longer crashes serial path (workers = 1, default) bootstrap replicates fail. failed replicate returned NULL list[[r]] <- NULL deleted element, shrinking result list triggering “missing value TRUE/FALSE needed”; documented drop--warn behaviour now works serial parallel paths. fit_me_calibration(), gls_combine(), compute_ise(), sigma_u_for_reliability(), build_sigma_u(), generate_aft_data() now validate inputs raise informative errors instead silently propagating NaN/Inf returning meaningless result: constant/-small validation samples, non-finite uninformative (zero-slope) surrogates, singular surrogate covariances, unsorted length-mismatched compute_ise() arguments, non-positive var_x/ratios/sigma_u_sq, --range rho, negative x_sd. Clarified serial (workers = 1) bootstrap canonical bit--bit reproducible path; parallel runs use independent L’Ecuyer streams reproducible across worker counts differ serial result seed design. Documentation: new applied-lpa article presenting dose-response applied scale – time-acceleration ratio light-physical-activity minutes, anchored 200 min/day reference, lower-support caveat two-stage vs single-stage interval-width comparison. quickstart simulation-study daily-scale section now use manuscript’s daily-LPA log scale (x_mean = log(300), x_sd = 0.45), correcting earlier raw-minute parameterisation. faq article gains parallel-execution / reproducibility note.

title: aftsplex 0.3.0
text: Realistic-scale data-generating process, two new simulation diagnostics, robustness pass bootstrap/SIMEX failure modes. generate_aft_data() gains x_mean, x_sd, f_args latent exposure dose-response can expressed meaningful scale (e.g. daily light-physical-activity minutes, mean ~300 150-minute threshold). defaults reproduce previous arbitrary-unit output bit--bit. New exported sigma_u_for_reliability() returns measurement-error covariance targeting given mean per-surrogate reliability, sweeping measurement quality (e.g. 0.5 / 0.65 / 0.8). simulation-study vignette gains “daily-minutes scale” section reliability sweep (Oracle / Naive / SIMEX ISE across reliability) per-surrogate ladder (surrogate alone vs GLS combiner via existing surrogate_pattern argument; engine change). Robustness pass (user hit -NA bootstrap curve message, opaque error plotting). two_stage_bootstrap() now isolates replicate degenerate resample drops NA instead aborting run, emits single summary warning (replicates dropped, grid points finite value, -NA point estimate, replicates failed). full-sample calibration gives clear message collinear/constant surrogates instead raw Lapack error, pointwise summaries NA-safe. simex_aft_spline() returns NA grid points converged perturbed fits (one summary warning) instead erroring “0 (non-NA) cases”; failed naive fit now gives informative error. plot_curves() drops entirely-NA curves warning stops clear message nothing left plot, instead empty panel. New “Troubleshooting” article documenting every warning/error message, “coverage diagnostics” article.
